correctness.rationale: RESULT.md lines 4–83: permutation averaging preserves all constraints and cannot increase the Fourier l1 norm even for complex values. A radial coefficient at layer j gives shell evaluations 1, 1-2j/n, and 1-4j(n-j)/(n(n-1)); at size two the character is negative exactly when one of the two coordinates lies in the subset, with probability 2j(n-j)/(n(n-1)). Hence the three signed moments are (1,0,Q) in (1,j,j(n-j)). Eliminate b_n via the first moment, writing X=(n-r)b_r and Y=(n-r-1)b_{r+1}; the other moments give X+Y=n and rX+(r+1)Y=Q. Thus X=n(r+1)-Q and Y=Q-nr have the stated signs; b_n<=0. The norm 1-2b_n yields the displayed value. At each integer j, the product (j-r)(j-r-1) is nonnegative and its upper bound is the larger convex endpoint value, D, because r<=(n-1)/2. Thus P_r is bounded in modulus by 1, with the required signed contacts; its pairing is exactly the claimed value by the moments, regardless of complex phases. This proves optimality over all admissible extensions, with at most three nonzero layers. Denominators are positive even for n=2. At a switch Q=nr, adjacent affine branches both take 1+2r/(n-r); D decreases across the switch, increasing the slope. A switch at d=2 is not interior, and at d=0 the optimizer is constant. Independent replay `python3 -I /workspace/review-work/replay.py 5` matched 186 exact grid optima through n=11, including switch targets, by enumerating Vandermonde-basis supports for the raw moments (1,0,-Q). For the real linear program split into positive and negative parts, an optimal basic solution has at most three nonzero signed entries, so this is an independent finite computation, not a proof of all dimensions and t. The supplied checker was inspected but not executed.

evidence: The positive-definite Hamming two-ball proof uses degree-two q-ary Krawtchouk polynomials and adjacent dual contacts, but maximizes counting mass of spatially supported functions with nonnegative Fourier data. The unrestricted Fourier signs are essential here: with sum j b_j=0, a nonnegative radial spectrum would have all its mass at j=0, forcing t=1. The inspected fourth-norm synthesis, concentration spectrum and tight-frame sampling sources respectively optimize a different quotient, a spectral conditioning problem and a Parseval identity with positive shell masses.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Changing primal positivity, spatial support and objective here is substantive. The positive-definite result does not cover t<1 and standard shell transforms only identify the constraints; none of the inspected statements supplies the closed signed-extension optimum.

evidence: In raw moments, sum b=1, sum j b=0 and sum j^2 b=-Q. Thus the dual tests the functional (coefficient of 1) minus Q times (coefficient of j^2) on quadratics bounded by 1 at integers 0,...,n. Equivalently, for quadratic regression on the same finite grid, a linear unbiased estimate of that functional has these signed weights b. Given b, minimizing its unit-noise variance factor sum b_j^2/p_j over design masses p_j by Cauchy–Schwarz gives (sum |b_j|)^2, attained with p proportional to |b|. Finite c-optimal design is therefore a genuine alternate formulation. The inspected four-moment Resultary record instead uses a continuous interval, four moments and a cubic certificate.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: This comparison credits the general minimum-total-variation formulation and finite design reduction without treating a generic LP algorithm, or a continuous cubic extremal theorem, as an explicit solution of the discrete adjacent-contact and staircase problem. A specialized c-optimal design or discrete Chebyshev classification remains a plausible equivalent.

value.rationale: For a natural Fourier-algebra interpolation problem on the first Boolean ball with a freely variable second-order profile, the minimum spectral l1 norm is the quantitative cost of enforcing these local data. The exact expression controls both that cost and the changing optimal signed layers, including arithmetic phase boundaries at all dimensions. This is not a single parameter slice or a generic LP existence result. No classification of all optimizers, higher Hamming data, or other alphabets is needed or implied.
